history.dynasty: None (guru-centred devotional tradition); HoraMata structure built 1721 AD by Raja Bhichchugatti Bharamanna, Palegar of Chitradurga, with Indo-Saracenic additions by Hyder Ali
history.period: 15th-16th century (Guru's lifetime; Karnataka HRCE Temple Information System suggests possibly 1570-1646 AD); Rajagopura of OlaMata ~200 years old
history.summary: Guru temple-cum-matha of Sri Guru Thipperudraswamy (Tippeswamy, c. 15th/16th century), a Shaivite guru and social reformer counted among the Pancha Ganadheeshwaras, revered by Hindu and Muslim devotees alike. He preached 'Kayakave Kailasa' (work is worship) and 'Madidastu Needu Bhikshe' (reward follows work), built reservoirs and paid women equal wages. Legend says his walking stick (Betta) and bag (Jolige) expelled the earlier local deity Mariamma from her shrine, which he converted into the present OlaMata Shiva temple (he installed a Shivalinga there). The outer HoraMata (1721 AD) houses his Jeeva Samadhi under an Islamic-style dome, a symbol of Hindu-Muslim unity; the Ekantha Mata 3 km away was his retreat. A unique custom is burning dry coconut (copra) and eating it as prasad. Lakhs attend the annual Jathra/Rathothsava.

name: Nayakanahatti Thipperudraswamy Temple
town_description: CSV town 'Chitradurga' corrected: the temple is at Nayakanahatti (also spelt Nayakanahatty), a village in Challakere taluk of Chitradurga district, about 35 km from the district headquarters Chitradurga. Originally called Nishadapura, it was renamed 'Nayakana Hatti' (the Leader's place) after Guru Thipperudraswamy settled there. It is a major pilgrimage centre drawing lakhs of devotees from Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana during the annual jathra. PIN 577536.

travel.road: On the Challakere-Nayakanahatti road; KSRTC buses from Chitradurga (~35 km)
